statement: The command tally shall read each file that the user names and print, for each file, the number of its lines, words and characters, and a total of them.
criterion: Given two text files with known counts, tally prints the line, word and character counts of each file and a total row whose counts are the sums of the per-file counts.

statement: The command shall accept the invocation tally [-l] [-w] [-c] [file...], with zero or more file names.
criterion: tally run with zero, one and three file names, each with and without any combination of -l, -w and -c, is accepted and exits 0 for readable valid UTF-8 input.

statement: The flag -l shall select the line count only, -w the word count only and -c the character count only; with no flag, the command shall print all three counts.
criterion: For a known file, tally -l prints only the line count, tally -w only the word count, tally -c only the character count, and tally with no flag prints the line, word and character counts.

statement: When no file name is given, the command shall read and count standard input.
criterion: Piping a text with known counts into tally with no file argument prints those counts for standard input and exits 0.

statement: The output shall have one row for each file, holding the counts that the flags select followed by the file name, each field separated from the next by exactly one space.
criterion: For a file a.txt with 2 lines, 3 words and 10 characters, tally a.txt prints exactly the row "2 3 10 a.txt", and tally -w a.txt prints exactly "3 a.txt".

statement: When two or more files are named, the last output row shall be the total row, labelled total, holding the sums of the selected counts.
criterion: tally a.txt b.txt prints three rows, the last ending in "total" with counts equal to the sums of the two file rows; tally a.txt prints no total row.

statement: A file that cannot be read shall produce a message on standard error naming the file and the reason, and the command shall exit with code 1.
criterion: tally on a missing file and on a file without read permission writes to standard error a message containing the file name and the reason (for example, no such file or permission denied) and exits 1.

statement: A file that cannot be read shall not stop the counting of the other named files.
criterion: tally good1.txt missing.txt good2.txt prints the count rows for good1.txt and good2.txt and the total row, writes an error for missing.txt to standard error, and exits 1.

statement: A file that is not valid UTF-8 shall produce a message on standard error naming the file, and the command shall exit with code 1.
criterion: tally on a file containing an invalid UTF-8 byte sequence (for example the byte 0xFF) writes a message containing the file name to standard error and exits 1.

statement: When no error occurs, the command shall exit with code 0.
criterion: tally on readable, valid UTF-8 files and on valid standard input exits 0.

statement: The product shall be written in Go using the standard library only and built with the Go toolchain.
criterion: go.mod declares no required modules, every import is from the Go standard library, and go build succeeds with the Go toolchain alone.

statement: The product shall provide no counts other than lines, words and characters, such as bytes, paragraphs or sentences.
criterion: The command accepts no flag other than -l, -w and -c, and its output contains only line, word and character counts.

statement: The product shall not read archives, directories or files that are not text.
criterion: The product contains no archive-extraction or directory-traversal code; a directory argument is not counted as text.

statement: The product shall provide no graphical interface, network service or plug-in system.
criterion: The product imports no GUI, network-server or plug-in package and runs only as a command-line program.

statement: The last line of a file shall be counted when the file does not end with a line feed.
criterion: The input "a\nb" counts 2 lines, the input "a" counts 1 line, and the empty input counts 0 lines.

statement: A word shall be counted as a run of characters that are not white space, where white space is any character with the Unicode property White_Space.
criterion: The input "a b\tc d e" counts 5 words, since the no-break space U+00A0 and the em space U+2003 have the White_Space property.

statement: A character shall be counted as one Unicode code point of UTF-8 text.
criterion: The input "héllo€" (one 2-byte and one 3-byte code point) counts 6 characters, not its 9 bytes.

statement: Counting a file of 10 MiB is fast.
criterion: At most 2 seconds of elapsed time on a computer with 4 cores, measured by a test that counts a generated file of 10 MiB (10,485,760 bytes) and measures the elapsed time.

statement: Counting a file of 1 GiB uses bounded memory.
criterion: At most 64 MiB of heap, measured by a test that counts a generated file of 1 GiB (1,073,741,824 bytes) and reads the heap size at the end.

statement: The counting package is thoroughly tested.
criterion: At least 90 percent statement coverage of the counting package, as reported by go test -cover.
